sections.overview: The great spotted woodpecker is a widespread Eurasian woodland bird.
sections.identification: Its black-and-white plumage includes white shoulder patches and red beneath the tail; males have a red nape and juveniles a red crown.
sections.habitat: It uses deciduous, coniferous and mixed woods, as well as wooded parks and gardens.
sections.diet: Its varied diet includes invertebrates, seeds and fruit; it searches bark and shallow wood for prey.
sections.behavior: It climbs trunks and branches and uses its bill to probe or hammer wood while feeding.
sections.reproduction: The pair excavates a nest cavity in a tree; both sexes take part in incubation and care of the young.
sections.ecology: In woodland management, retaining dead and dying trees preserves important feeding resources for this woodpecker.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists the species globally as Least Concern, while reporting a decreasing population trend in its 2026 factsheet.
